title: Comparing characteristic-p and characteristic-zero fibres
quote: Ils ne sont en général pas isomorphes; sans doute; Vérifier
context: Adds to CT54/003,005,007 (de Rham and Cartier-duality comparisons); no matching general mixed-characteristic assertion
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; no dedicated mixed-characteristic comparison entry
body: The displayed extension of the characteristic-zero realization to \(W(k)\) already puts the comparison over a common coefficient ring; the remaining question is whether an isomorphism preserves only the tensor realization or also semilinear and Frobenius data. The finite-residue-field qualification is partly deleted and uncertain, and the cancelled “Vérifier” is no evidence of a completed check. Oda (1969, Corollary 5.11) supplies a precise degree-one comparison in characteristic p, not a classification of these mixed-characteristic comparisons.

title: Two filtrations with different origins
quote: ne provient pas d’une filtration du motif
context: Adds to CT54/003,005 and CN D01–D02; their Hodge exact sequence is a concrete instance, not a definition of this manuscript’s second filtration
body: The margin distinguishes a filtration intrinsic to the motive from the Hodge filtration of its de Rham realization. Its displayed associated-graded description contains the uncertain coefficient reading \(\mathbf Q_l\), which must remain a reading question rather than become a retrospectively corrected de Rham formula. The earlier effectivity and mixed-extension leads do not fix either convention on this sheet.

title: Semilinear descent does not supply monodromy
quote: Il n’y a plus en général d’opération de π₁(X)
context: Adds to CT54/003’s de Rham realization; differs from CT16/019–023’s étale cohomological setting
body: The pages repeatedly separate automorphisms of the coefficient field acting semilinearly from a fundamental-group action on a fibre. A comparison argument must therefore specify its base point, scalar extension and descent datum before transporting an action. This distinction limits any attempt to read the later discrete motivic group as an already-defined topological or étale fundamental group.

title: The cohomological degree of the fibre-functor obstruction
quote: une classe de coh dans H^{2|1}
context: Adds to CT54/003’s extension-class discussion; no matching fibre-functor obstruction formula in CT
body: The frozen exponent is explicitly uncertain between 2 and 1. Once a fibre functor is fixed, its forms are classified by nonabelian \(H^1\); neutralizing the gerbe is a different obstruction problem (Deligne & Milne, 1982/2012, §§2–3). This gives a contextual reason to revisit the ink in a future edition, not permission to change the frozen exponent or assert which obstruction was intended.

title: Absence of a canonical rational comparison
quote: il n’y a pas d’isom canonique prévisible
context: Adds to CT54/003,007 and Oda1969’s characteristic-p comparison; differs in base field and coefficient ring
body: The text distinguishes non-canonicity from the stronger possibility that no isomorphism exists over \(\mathbf Q_l\). A later comparison after adjoining a period ring does not establish an isomorphism over that original coefficient field, and an integral lattice is additional data. The marginal restriction to weight and level zero singles out a smaller case whose descent data still have to be specified.

title: Archimedean places and integral Betti comparison
quote: isom canonique “involutif”
context: Adds to CT54/003,005’s de Rham duality by specifying an integral Betti lattice and conjugation
ledger: LM7 C.1 [Known, return’s claim]; MPL_14_002-044 M24a [first-pass lead]
body: The page identifies the Betti lattice after extension to \(\mathbf Z_l\) or \(\mathbf C\), and then explains why a conjugate complex point gives an involutively related lattice. That comparison does not say that the lattice alone recovers the archimedean place. The distinction becomes explicit in the retraction on scans 207 and 225.

title: The two semilinear conjugations
quote: τ = τ′τ″ = τ″τ′; à vérifier
context: Adds to CT54/003,005; no two-conjugation identity located in CT
body: The author marks the commuting-product identity itself for verification. A proof must compare conjugation induced by the Betti real form with conjugation induced by real de Rham descent under the chosen comparison isomorphism. Two semilinear involutions have a linear product, but their commutativity does not follow merely from semilinearity.

title: Real Frobenius compatibility
quote: frobenius en la place réelle; à vérifier
context: Adds to CT54/007’s Frobenius–Verschiebung diagram; differs by using archimedean conjugation rather than characteristic-p Frobenius
body: The second verification mark concerns the identification of the real involution with the corresponding action on an l-adic fibre. The later continuation asserts the resulting integral action of \(f_\infty\), but supplies no separate compatibility proof. The archimedean operator is not thereby identified with a finite-field Frobenius.

title: Hodge theory as a motivic-level conjecture
quote: La partie de niveau; le dernier sous-espace … est motivique
context: Adds to CT16/044,049 and CT44/004,008–009; these discuss algebraicity and positivity, not this intersection formula
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M01, M29a [first-pass leads]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]
body: The formula proposes that an intersection involving the rational Betti realization, a Hodge-filtration term and its \(f_\infty\)-translate comes from a submotive, although the individual Hodge terms do not. The uncertain level index and the meaning of “niveau” must be fixed before identifying this with a particular generalized Hodge conjecture. Grothendieck (1969b, §1) explicitly distinguishes the rational algebraic-class conjecture from a stronger filtration statement requiring correction; that printed discussion is relevant without establishing an exact equivalence with this draft.

title: The rational-subspace test for the level formula
quote: provient d’un sous-motif
context: Adds a test to CT16/049’s subobject/splitting programme and CN S14–S16
body: Before using the displayed intersection as a motivic subobject, test that its complexification is stable under the Hodge decomposition, not merely under conjugation. A submotive would have that stability, while an arbitrary rational subspace lying in a band of Hodge types need not have it. Confidence: high for this necessary-condition test, because functoriality of a Hodge realization forces subobjects to be Hodge substructures; no geometric counterexample to the manuscript’s undefined level convention is asserted.

title: Retraction of separation by bare integral or real fibres
quote: Je pense; faux, cf groupoïde fondamental sur Z; très loin d’être caractérisée
context: Adds a documented internal retraction; CT contains no parallel archimedean-place separation claim
body: The claim that distinct places always yield non-isomorphic integral or real fibre functors is explicitly marked “faux” on scan 207. Scans 219–221 supply finite-type and countable-field isomorphism arguments, and scan 225 restates the failure of place recovery from the bare \(\mathbf Z\)-module functor. The later number-field separation question is narrower and remains distinct from this withdrawn unrestricted assertion.

title: Real neutralization in positive characteristic
quote: T_α(R)=∅ pour α grand; Vérifier … ext. tot. réelle ???
context: Adds to CT54/005,007’s positive-characteristic realization problems; no matching real-neutralization assertion found
body: The expectation is the nonexistence of real-valued fibre functors for sufficiently large finite pieces of the category, with a separate question about totally real extensions. It requires an actual obstruction to real neutralization, not merely the absence of a geometric complex-conjugation operation in characteristic p. The sheet gives neither the required finite subcategory nor an obstruction class.

title: A gerbe of points and individual path torsors
quote: catégorie fibrée … fpqc; c’est un torseur; classes de chemins
context: Adds to CT54/003’s universal-extension language; no equivalent fibre-functor gerbe construction in CT
body: Between two fibre functors, tensor isomorphisms form a torsor when locally nonempty; the category of fibre functors is a gerbe (Deligne & Milne, 1982/2012, §3). The manuscript moves from “catégorie fibrée” to “torseur” without spelling out that distinction. A reconstruction should keep its groupoid of points and its individual path objects separate.

title: Twisting a fixed motivic point
quote: tous les autres pts s’en déduisent par des fibrés principaux
context: Adds to CT54/003’s extension classification; the torsor classification here is a different construction
body: The assertion is a descent statement relative to one fibre functor and its affine tensor-automorphism group. Its integral version requires exactness, local freeness and an appropriate reconstruction theorem over the chosen ring; the neutral Tannakian theorem over a field cannot by itself justify every ring-valued case. This is the structural prerequisite for the later proposed classification of places by torsors.

title: The proposed bijection with enriched transcendental points
quote: Il semble … biunivoquement; structure supplémentaire
context: Adds to CT16/049’s category-level programme; no such bijection in CT
body: The bracketed “structure supplémentaire” is decisive: the proposed bijection cannot be read as the bare-lattice statement already marked false. Scans 225–227 later ask which Hodge-valued tensor functors are geometric. The unspecified enrichment is therefore part of the open question, not a completed classification.

title: Crystalline points as a reconstruction problem
quote: Questions; À revoir; avec structure supplémentaire (F,V)
context: Adds to CT54/005,007; restates the need to retain F,V while enlarging the problem from abelian degree one to motives
body: The page is headed “Questions” and marked “À revoir”, so the arrows from geometric points to filtered or crystalline motivic points are proposals. Oda’s degree-one result identifies the relevant Dieudonné module and Hodge sequence for an abelian variety over a perfect field, but does not classify arbitrary motives by a Witt-valued point with two operators (Oda, 1969, Corollary 5.11). The base field’s perfection and the integral versus isogeny setting must remain explicit.

title: Filtered points in characteristic zero
quote: correspondent aux pts motiviques dans h, avec structure filtrée
context: Adds to CT54/003’s filtered de Rham sequence; no essential-image criterion there
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 M01, M29a [first-pass leads]; WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]
body: The proposed correspondence needs an essential-image condition, since a filtered fibre functor alone does not include all geometric, rational and positivity constraints. The later explicit essential-image question on scan 227 confirms that this is not a theorem proved by the tabular arrows. A modern comparison should specify whether the target includes Betti data, polarization, Griffiths transversality or an admissibility condition.

title: A discrete automorphism group is not automatically π₁ top
quote: Groupe fondamental motivique discret; Comparaison avec π₁
context: Adds to CT16/049; differs from CT16/047, where π₁ denotes a cohomological Künneth projector, not a fundamental group
body: The definition is \(\operatorname{Aut}^{\otimes}(\xi)=G_\xi(\mathbf Z)\), followed by a question of comparison with the topological fundamental group. A monodromy homomorphism into this automorphism group need not be injective or surjective. In particular, the \(\pi_1\) occurring in the context’s discussion of algebraic projectors must not be used as evidence for a fundamental-group identification.

title: Arithmetic finiteness needs a specified orbit problem
quote: En vertu de Borel\inserted{-\unsure{Harish}}; nb fini
context: Adds to CT16/049’s finite-dimensional semisimplicity discussion; no Borel–Harish-Chandra application found in CT
body: The intended finiteness concerns isomorphism classes of integral fibre functors. Arithmetic orbit finiteness could be the intended input, but the page does not identify the finite-type group, integral representation, closed orbit or class-number problem to which Borel and Harish-Chandra (1962) would apply. The uncertainty in the inserted name remains, and the further question whether the resulting discrete groups are isomorphic is separate from finiteness of the set of forms.

title: Full faithfulness from Hodge and Tate
quote: est … fidèle; conjonction des conj. de Hodge et de Tate
context: Adds to CT16/049’s semisimple-motives yoga and CT44/008’s realization proposals
ledger: MPL_14_087-132 M09 [first-pass lead]; WG2 §2.3 #7, WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plans]
body: The functor includes an action of the manuscript’s discrete motivic automorphism group together with a Hodge structure on the fibre; comparison with the topological fundamental group is itself raised as a question. Its asserted full faithfulness is conditional on Hodge and finite-field Tate conjectures, at least for normal X, and would need a precise category of relative motives and a spreading or specialization argument. Tate’s finite-field abelian-variety Hom theorem is a narrower input (Tate, 1966).

title: The essential image remains open
quote: Caractériser l’image ??
context: Adds to CT16/049’s categorical expectation; no essential-image characterization found
body: Full faithfulness, even if granted, does not identify which representations of this discrete motivic group with Hodge data are realizations of motives. The double question mark asks precisely for this missing image condition. Scans 217 and 227 suggest moduli of polarized motives as an approach without resolving it.

title: Serre’s conjugate-variety example is a test, not the ring example
quote: Analyser l’exemple de Serre de π₁ non isomorphes
context: Adds to CT16/047’s different Serre objection to a hypersurface reduction; the two uses of Serre concern different claims
body: The author asks to analyze conjugate varieties with non-isomorphic topological fundamental groups. That property does not, on its own, imply that their integral cohomology rings differ, which is the stronger criterion sought on scan 223. Charles (2009, introduction and Theorem 1) explicitly separates the earlier fundamental-group examples from the later cohomology-algebra construction.

title: Real descent and generation by real Frobenius
quote: avec la comp. conn. … engendre G; pleinement fidèle
context: Adds to CT44/004,008–009’s positivity programme; no corresponding real-descent generation assertion
body: The page claims that real Frobenius together with the connected component generates the motivic group, and that Hodge structure plus the indicated realification is fully faithful. These depend on identifying the component quotient and the relevant descent category, in addition to the Hodge assertion. The correction from “géom. connexe” to “irred (pas néc. géom irred)” must be retained as an explicit change of hypothesis, not silently strengthened back.

title: Recovering a variation from one fibre
quote: étudier comment varie la structure de Hodge
context: Adds to CT44/002,004’s polarized abelian-variety programme and CT47/003’s relative setup
body: The question asks how the Hodge structure varies from a fixed fibre, and the geometric setting has a precise rigidity mechanism: Deligne’s fixed-part result keeps a global flat section that has one Hodge type at one point in that type everywhere (Deligne, 1971, Corollary 4.1.2 and §4.1.3.1). Applied to a Hom variation, it explains why a monodromy-compatible fibre morphism can remain Hodge-compatible throughout a connected algebraic base under the theorem’s hypotheses. The note should therefore be pursued through geometric polarizable variations, not treated as a general counterexample-producing assertion about arbitrary analytic local systems.

title: Rigidity of a map to a motivic moduli space
quote: déterminé … en un point, plus l’application π₁
context: Adds to CT47/003’s abelian-scheme setting and CT44/004’s polarization; no stated map-rigidity theorem in CT
body: The assertion fixes both the value of a map and its induced fundamental-group map. In the abelian-scheme case, the fixed-part argument extends a fibre homomorphism compatible with monodromy to the family (Deligne, 1971, §4.1.3.2), providing a concrete model for the proposed rigidity. Extending this to arbitrary polarized motives still requires the moduli problem and realization/fullness hypotheses to be specified.

title: Characterizing varieties by motivic rigidity
quote: Peut-être … interprétées comme … variétés modulaires
context: Adds to CT16/049’s categorical yoga; no moduli characterization in CT
body: The author asks whether varieties possessing the stated rigidity property can all be interpreted as moduli spaces of certain motifs. This is an inverse construction problem, distinct from proving rigidity for a known moduli space. Its quantifier “toutes” and the unresolved class of permitted motifs should be recorded before seeking special cases.

title: Motivically pointed schemes
quote: Introduire la notion de schéma … pointé
context: Adds to CT16/049’s category programme and CT47/003’s base-scheme functoriality
body: The proposed base point is a fibre functor valued in an arbitrary ring h, giving a tensor-automorphism group and its h-points. To define the induced group homomorphism, the morphism of pointed schemes must include a compatible identification of fibre functors. Forgetting that identification leaves an inner-conjugacy ambiguity, which matters when comparing the construction with anabelian Hom statements.

title: Finite tensor subcategories versus one global isomorphism
quote: pour tte sous-catégorie … de t.f.
context: Adds to CT16/049’s finite-dimensional correspondence arguments; no compatible-system assertion in CT
body: The sheet explicitly asks two different questions: isomorphism of the full fibre functors, and separate isomorphisms on every finitely generated tensor subcategory. Passing from the latter to the former requires compatible choices in an inverse system of isomorphism torsors. The distinction explains why the subsequent countability argument is mathematically substantive.

title: Spreading out the finite-subcategory comparison
quote: grâce au groupoïde fondamental transcendant
context: Adds a Betti-path method to CT16/045–046’s specialization arguments; differs from their algebraic-cycle conclusions
body: When the places agree on the algebraic part of the field, the sketch spreads X and a finite tensor subcategory to a finite-type model and appeals to a connected complex groupoid. A complete proof must show that the chosen motifs, their tensor relations and the required integral comparison all descend to that model. Normality and geometric connectedness are written ingredients and should not disappear in a reformulation.

title: The countable inverse limit of path sets
quote: les morphismes de transition … sont surjectifs; on gagne
context: Adds to CT16/045–046’s reduction techniques; no matching countable inverse-path argument in CT
body: The sketch reduces to a sequence of smooth models with geometrically connected fibres and claims surjectivity on path classes. Nonempty sets with surjective maps in a countable inverse system admit a compatible sequence by successive choices, but obtaining that particular system of models and those surjections remains the geometric step. The uncertain superscript on π is retained and cannot be used to decide whether the intended groupoid is topological or completed.

title: The uncountable case is unfinished
quote: Si k pas dénombrable,
context: Adds an explicit boundary to CT16/045–046’s finite reduction pattern; no uncountable construction located
body: The phrase ends without an argument. It marks the scope limit of the preceding countable construction rather than proving either failure or success for uncountable fields. No compactness or inverse-limit theorem is supplied to remove that limit.

title: Separation on the algebraic part of the field
quote: je pense qu’il existe α
context: Adds to CT16/049’s finite motivic pieces; narrows the withdrawn unrestricted assertion of15/207
body: For places differing on the algebraic part E, the author expects a finitely generated tensor subcategory on which the integral fibre functors differ. The reduction to a number field is stated, but the frozen \(\operatorname{Spec}(E|k)\) and surrounding field notation remain uncertain. An existence example of one conjugate pair does not prove this separation for every pair.

title: A multiplicative cohomology witness
quote: non isomorphes comme anneaux; remplacer Z par R??
context: Adds to CT16/015–018’s correspondence-ring emphasis; no conjugate cohomology-ring example in CT
body: A tensor isomorphism of fibre functors must preserve the multiplication morphism of a cohomology algebra object, so a non-isomorphic graded ring is a suitable witness even when the underlying groups agree. Charles (2009, Theorems 1–2) constructs smooth projective conjugates over a number field with non-isomorphic real cohomology algebras, answering the existential real-coefficient version of the margin’s question. This does not establish universal separation of prescribed places or identify those examples with the ones Serre was asked to provide.

title: Injectivity of the place-to-torsor map
quote: si M est pris assez grand
context: Adds to CT16/049’s finite-category programme; no place-to-torsor injection in CT
body: The conjecture asserts that a sufficiently large motive separates archimedean places through the isomorphism classes of associated integral torsors. The qualification on M is essential: a small realization can forget places. One must also decide whether a single M is meant to separate all places at once and specify the integral group scheme attached to it.

title: Surjectivity onto all torsors
quote: ∀ fibré principal homogène P … provient d’une place
context: Adds to CT16/049’s reconstruction programme; no arithmetic torsor-surjectivity theorem in CT
body: This is stronger than injectivity and is immediately qualified by the marginal Riemann–Hodge compatibility warning. The appropriate target may be torsors equipped with a complex comparison satisfying positivity and Hodge constraints, rather than every unadorned torsor under the integral group. The manuscript asks the question but does not define that restricted target.

title: Different torsors need not imply non-isomorphic abstract groups
quote: ces groupes à priori ne sont pas isomorphes
context: Adds a logical test to CT16/049’s group/category discussion; no abstract-group classification in CT
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan]; the distinct GL₂ uniqueness issue in LM1 A.8 is treated separately in M11
body: Separate the torsor-class comparison from the abstract isomorphism problem for the groups of integral points of the twisted automorphism groups. The first does not formally settle the second, since forgetting a group scheme, tensors or its action loses information. Confidence: high for this distinction, because an isomorphism of abstract groups is a weaker structure than an isomorphism of the specified tensor torsors; no specific counterexample to the manuscript’s arithmetic setting is claimed.

title: Does Hodge enrichment recover the place?
quote: que se passe-t-il … structures de Hodge ?
context: Adds to CT54/003,005’s Hodge data and CT16/049’s motive category; no geometric essential-image theorem in CT
body: The question deliberately restores the Hodge structure after the failure of the bare integral functor. The margin warns that a complex place must be specified appropriately for that structure, so quotienting by conjugation and forgetting it are not interchangeable operations. The deleted reduction through the projective line supplies no proof of the general reconstruction; X02–X03 give a separate conditional argument for ordinary complex points and chosen field embeddings when the integral Hodge lattice is retained.

title: The elliptic j-family as a test case
quote: Il semble qu’on le verrait facilement; invariant … j
context: Adds a proposed family to CT54/003,005 and CT44/008’s abelian realizations
body: The proposed test is mathematically natural when j denotes the normalized invariant \(j_{\mathrm{classical}}/1728\), since the three omitted values are then 0, 1 and infinity. Existence of one elliptic family does not require a universal family on a fine moduli scheme, although a universal moduli interpretation requires the usual rigidification. The invariant normalization, integral lattice data and meaning of Hodge-functor recovery must be fixed before claiming that this example proves the general statement; X01–X03 give an explicit family and the precise injectivity test it supports.

title: Reconstructing maps from tensor functors
quote: dans quelle mesure … un foncteur … peut-il être pris arbitrairement ?!?
context: Adds to CT16/049’s categorical yoga; no anabelian Hom assertion in CT
body: The page asks both faithfulness of the passage from scheme maps to motivic tensor functors and characterization of its image. These are distinct from the Tate comparison of linear Hom spaces and from an anabelian theorem for specified hyperbolic curves. The marginal appeal to Hodge is a proposed input, not a proof covering arbitrary preschemes.

title: The proposed moduli immersion criterion
quote: Y … Modules est une immersion; \unsure{anabélien}
context: Adds to CT44/004,008’s polarization programme; no moduli-immersion criterion in CT
body: The proposed implication would use a global polarized motive on Y and an immersive map to a moduli space to recover maps into Y. The uncertain word “anabélien”, the kind of immersion and the class of source schemes all need clarification before this can be treated as an anabelian statement. The last sentence about spectra of fields is an expectation without a proof on this sheet.

title: Reused Lie-theory text is not motivic evidence
quote: ALGÈBRES de LIE SEMI-SIMPLES; représentations de sl₂
context: Differs from CT16/006–018’s Lefschetz operators; CT54/008 provides a parallel instance of reused root-system text
body: These are editorial/typescript sheets from another text, with Tribu and rédaction numbers. Their occurrence of \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), Cartan and roots is not evidence that the handwritten motivic Galois group contains the Lefschetz action. The heading and reuse classification must remain attached to any mathematical quotation from these leaves.

title: Finite-dimensional hypotheses in the representation text
quote: Ajouter “de dim. finie”; pas si “facile”
context: Differs from CT16/006–018’s graded Lefschetz algebra; supplies an independent editorial restriction
ledger: WG2 §2.3 #2 [unchecked plan, analogy only; no topical settled entry]
body: The reused editorial sheet repeatedly adds finite-dimensionality and replaces an allegedly easy argument by a Casimir calculation. These changes identify a missing hypothesis and a deferred proof in the source being revised. They do not supply a proof of semisimplicity for a motivic category.

title: An explicitly unchecked rank formula
quote: Vérifier la formule du bas de la p. 9
context: Differs from CT54/008’s root-system fragment; the referenced p.9 is not supplied
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no mathematical result ID]
body: The editorial instruction explicitly requests verification of a formula on a different page. That target page is absent, so the formula cannot be reconstructed from the instruction. This is a genuine unverified-step entry even though it belongs to reused typescript.

title: Characteristic-two and positive-characteristic corrections
quote: ne sont vraies qu’en caract. ≠2; fausse en caract. p
context: Differs from CT16/014’s separate integral Lefschetz issue; no identical correction in CT
body: The sheet withdraws a characteristic-free formulation, citing nilpotence of \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) in characteristic 2, then orders two further false positive-characteristic assertions removed or replaced. Their original statements lie on unsupplied pages 10, 15 and the indicated final remark, so only the corrections themselves are witnessed here. All corrections are on scan 202; no later motivic theorem is being retracted.

title: Deleted source propositions and a corrected summation
quote: c’est faux; la sommation est incorrecte
context: Differs from CT54/008’s root-system page; referenced source pp.1–5 are absent
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no topical result ID]
body: The editorial text rejects specified propositions and instructs that a summation run over half the roots. Without the referenced earlier pages, one cannot reconstruct the original false statements or determine all hypotheses of the replacement. The record therefore preserves the withdrawal and correction without assigning them to the motivic discussion.

title: Root-definition symbols retained literally
context: Restates the root-system subject of CT54/008 but differs in the displayed definitions
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no topical result ID]
body: The frozen typescript formulas do not match the expected typed expression \([h,x]=\alpha(h)x\): one lacks a visible α before \((a)\), and the other has \(\alpha(x)\). Since x lies in the Lie algebra rather than necessarily in the Cartan domain of α, this is a mathematical type check and a future source-collation question. No missing symbol is supplied to the transcription.

title: The domain condition for local associativity
quote: m(x,m(y,z)) appartiennent à Ω
context: Differs from CT16/025’s explicitly boxed associativity conditions; both show why the domain must be specified
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no topical result ID]
body: The fourth listed member of Ω is a product value in G, although Ω was defined as a subset of \(G\times G\). The likely mathematical condition concerns the pair \((x,m(y,z))\), but this is an editorial interpretation of a type mismatch, not a corrected reading. The following inverse calculation also retains its written parenthesis structure.

title: Deferred extensions to group germs
quote: Nous laisserons au lecteur le soin d’étendre
context: Adds a separate reuse example alongside CT16/033–037 and CT54/008; no matching group-germ proof in CT
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no topical result ID]
body: The typescript leaves three sets of extensions to the reader: propositions 3 and 3 bis, the notation and results of nos.12–16, and propositions 11–12 with corollaries. A completion would have to control the domains of partially defined multiplication and the loss from \(C^r\) to \(C^{r-1}\) on tangent objects. These are deferred proofs in the reused source, not new conjectures about motives.

title: A later unimodularity theorem is only announced
quote: Nous verrons plus tard … semi-simples ou nilpotents
context: Differs from CT16/049’s motivic semisimplicity; the shared adjective does not identify the assertions
body: The reused Haar-measure text announces unimodularity of connected semisimple or nilpotent Lie groups. The determinant expression on scan 218 suggests the missing proof through the adjoint modular character, but the promised later argument is absent. Unimodularity is not centre-freeness or semisimplicity of a tensor category.

title: Formal maps and coalgebra compatibility
quote: applications diagonales; a_{0,0}≠0
context: Differs from CT54/007’s finite-group-scheme/restricted-Lie comparison; the reused page concerns formal-map coalgebras
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no topical result ID]
body: The proposition characterizes formal maps by a condition on the degree-zero part and compatibility with the diagonal. Its proof switches from modules M and N to M and M′, and writes \(a_{0,0}\ne0\), so the coefficient-ring assumptions and the meaning of equality of degree-zero submodules should be recovered from the missing preceding source. These notational issues do not establish an identification with the crystalline operators on scan 5.

title: Bibliographic reuse and dating
quote: Page 6; Proposal to National Science Foundation; To Appear, Summer 1969
context: Restates the codicological problem of CT16/028’s reused bibliography and CN16:28:1; differs in source and listed work
ledger: WG2 §1.1 #3 [unchecked organizational plan; no topical result ID]
body: The printed bibliography contains dated and forthcoming approximation-theory items, but its author is not named on this sheet. Those dates can constrain the preparation of the reused source only after bibliographic identification; they do not by themselves date the handwritten Hodge or period sheets. Its printed page 6 and visible manuscript number 2 are separate pagination systems.
